content_of_post_to_comment: Wouldn’t it be incredible if instead of teaching kids about mitochondria and sines and cosines in high school we taught them basic landscaping, cooking, plumbing, electric, car maintenance, childcare, carpentry, personal finance, sewing. etc? I just think it would make for better functioning adults.
comment: The interesting tradeoff is not practical skills versus theory, but whether schools should teach transfer skills: how to learn, adapt, and solve unfamiliar problems when life demands something not on the syllabus.
